solution.operation: Set up the division using Paravartya Yojayet method
solution.description: We are dividing a cubic polynomial by a linear factor. The divisor is (x - 2), so we use the root x = 2 for the Paravartya method.

solution.operation: Write coefficients of dividend and the root
solution.description: Write the coefficients of the dividend (1, 7, 6, 5) and the root (2) from the divisor (x - 2). Bring down the first coefficient (1).
Multiply the root (2) by the first coefficient (1) to get 2. Add to the next coefficient: 7 + 2 = 9.
Multiply the root (2) by the previous result (9) to get 18. Add to the next coefficient: 6 + 18 = 24.
Multiply the root (2) by the previous result (24) to get 48. Add to the last coefficient: 5 + 48 = 53. This is the remainder.
The coefficients (1, 9, 24) give the quotient polynomial, and the last number (53) is the remainder.

common_mistakes: Using -2 as the multiplier because the divisor is written x - 2; the Paravartya step transposes the sign, so 2 is what gets multiplied down.
Treating the final number 53 as another quotient coefficient instead of as the remainder, giving a cubic quotient rather than the quadratic x squared plus 9x plus 24.

solution.operation: Eliminate y (set y=0) and factor the resulting expression in x and z
solution.description: By setting y=0, we get a quadratic in x and z which factors to (2x + z)(x + 3z)

solution.operation: Combine the factors using the Vedic method
solution.description: Line the two partial factorisations up against each other. The z-free pair gives 2x + 3y and x + 2y, and the y-free pair gives 2x + z and x + 3z, and the leading terms 2x and x match across both, so the missing variable can be slotted into each bracket.

Assemble each full factor by taking its share from both partial results: the bracket that carried 2x and 3y also carries the z from the second partial factorisation, giving 2x + 3y + z, and the other bracket becomes x + 2y + 3z.
Expanding the factors confirms we get back the original expression, verifying our factorization is correct.
